title: Tracking Things That Move: A Constant Velocity Filter for Each Object, Association by Distance, and the Three Ways It Goes Wrong

questions.question: Why does a planner need a velocity as well as a position of a person?
options: To identify the person again later
To filter the noise of the position
It needs where they will be, and a position alone is where they were
To know how large the person is
questions.explanation: By the time the vehicle acts, the person has moved. The velocity is what turns a position now into a position then.

questions.question: The velocity error of the difference of two positions was:
options: 0.7 m/s exactly
questions.explanation: Two positions each good to 5 cm, 0.1 s apart, give a velocity good to no better than 0.7 m/s. The filter, using all the past, got 0.122 m/s.

questions.question: A track was confirmed after how many frames?
questions.explanation: A track is tentative until it has been seen three times. A single false detection was a tentative track for one frame and then gone.

questions.question: A target hidden for 8 frames came out with:
options: The same id, having coasted
A new id: the track had been dropped
No track at all
The id of the nearest other track
questions.explanation: A confirmed track coasts on its prediction for a few missed frames. Two frames behind a post kept the id; eight were too many.

questions.question: How well was the position 2 s ahead of a walking person predicted?
options: To within 0.02 m
To within 1.4 m
To within 0.20 m
To within 2.8 m, the distance walked
questions.explanation: At 1.4 m/s the person moved 2.8 m in that time, and the track's velocity put them within 0.20 m of where they were.

questions.question: Why can two targets that stop side by side swap ids?
options: When they are close the detections of one are nearer the prediction of the other
The filter's velocity is reset when they stop
Their detections merge into one
The tracker runs out of ids
questions.explanation: Standing 5 cm apart with 5 cm of noise, a detection is as near one prediction as the other. In 20 runs that swapped the ids 5 times.
